no_source_form.why: Go has no tagged union.
Go has no statement that leaves a function with a value of another package's type to the framework that started it.
Go has no unit type: a call of a function without results reads as an empty tuple.
Rust has no variadic function.
Rust has no variadic function to pass a slice to as its last parameter.
Rust has no statement that defers a call to the function's return: a drop guard is a value of a type written for it, dropped at the end of its scope.
Rust has no unary plus.
Java has no &^=; a &= ~b is assign.and of unop.complement.
Java has no defined type over a primitive or String; a class is a struct.
Java has no &^; a & ~b is op.and of unop.complement.
Java has no assignment of several targets at once.
Java has no statement that defers a call to the method's return: a finally block runs a fixed block, not the calls deferred at run time, last first.
Java has no channels.
A Java local has no zero value: javac rejects reading one that was never assigned.
Java has no fixed-size array type: an array's length belongs to the object, not to its type.
Java has no channels.
Java has no pointer to a local; an object reference is dereferenced implicitly.
Java has no channels.
C has no interface type.
C has no generic function or type.
C has no interface type to call a method through.
C has no generic function or type to give type arguments to.
C has no function literal.
C has no method value bound to its receiver: that is a closure.
C has no interface type to convert a value to.
C has no construct that makes a call when the function returns.
C has no statement that leaves every caller with a value.
C has no type parameter.
